purpose: Ropinirole is used to treat Parkinson's disease by helping control tremors, stiffness, and movement problems. It is also used to treat Restless Legs Syndrome (RLS), a condition where you feel an uncomfortable urge to move your legs, especially at night. It helps reduce those uncomfortable sensations so you can sleep and move more comfortably.
how_it_works: Your brain uses a chemical called dopamine to help control smooth, coordinated movement. In Parkinson's disease, your brain does not make enough dopamine. Ropinirole works by mimicking dopamine — it attaches to the same spots in your brain that dopamine would normally attach to, tricking your brain into thinking it has enough dopamine so your body can move more normally.
common_side_effects: Nausea or upset stomach (especially when you first start taking it), dizziness or lightheadedness, sleepiness or feeling very drowsy, headache, swelling in your legs or feet, and constipation. Some people feel dizzy when they stand up quickly, so take your time when getting up.
warnings: Ropinirole can make you very sleepy and has caused some people to fall asleep suddenly without warning, even while driving — do not drive until you know how this medication affects you. It can cause or worsen hallucinations (seeing or hearing things that are not there), especially in older adults. Some people develop strong urges they cannot control, such as gambling, eating, shopping, or sexual urges — tell your doctor right away if this happens. Do not stop this medication suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can cause serious withdrawal symptoms. Avoid alcohol as it increases drowsiness.
typical_dosing: For Parkinson's disease, you usually start with a low dose taken three times a day with meals to reduce nausea, and your doctor will slowly increase it over several weeks to find the right dose for you. For Restless Legs Syndrome, you typically take one dose one to three hours before bedtime. The extended-release tablet (Requip XL) is taken once a day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as doses vary from person to person.
